correctness.rationale: The theorem specifies all feasible integer run-count domains and the exact null distribution. A uniform-composition covariance formula for run lengths gives the even and odd conditional variances. Independent symbolic algebra verifies both formulas and the four difference identities, whose strictly positive feasible-domain substitutions prove the all-size claims, including boundary counts. Independent whole-word enumeration through length 15 and a larger exact rational grid corroborate them; neither finite check is presented as infinite proof. The packaged verifier reproduces 87811 assertions with explicit failure on mismatch.

evidence: Classical exact inversion variance is \(ab(a+b+1)/12\); it is recovered by averaging the new conditional variances but cannot determine them separately.

Known joint squared-rank-sum and total-run covariance is a single weighted average of the new variance profile, and therefore does not imply each conditional value or all neighboring strict comparisons.

Run-composition counting (arxiv:1410.8167) and inversion moment enumeration (arxiv:0908.2089) are distinct pieces of input; deriving the all-parameter parity-sawtooth requires additional mixed-moment algebra and positive-polynomial factorization.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier covariance identity and unconditional variance are consequences or aggregates of the conditional theorem, not stronger covering statements. The theorem is strictly more informative because it decides each feasible adjacent and same-parity conditional comparison for every composition. Its significance is not premised on rediscovering the marginal identities.

originality.rationale: The contribution is the exact run-conditioned second-moment profile and complete strict parity-sawtooth inequalities. The Gaussian-binomial inversion literature supplies unconditional moments, and classical two-color run theory supplies run counts, but neither states the mixed conditioning theorem. An earlier exact mixed covariance is substantially weaker and does not determine this conditional profile; the accessible comparison found no covering stronger theorem. Historical implicit coverage in older joint run-rank work remains a priority risk, not a demonstrated counterexample to novelty.
residual_risks: An older text giving the complete *joint* law of inversions and total runs may implicitly encode the conditional moments; no exact covering inequality theorem was found in the accessible primary comparisons.

value.rationale: The Wilcoxon/Mann–Whitney rank sum and the Wald–Wolfowitz total runs are two canonical, jointly observable distribution-free two-sample statistics. An earlier zero covariance of the raw statistics conceals nonconstant conditional dispersion. The exact sharp all-size parity-sawtooth, including an odd-run strict local minimum between neighboring even-run variances, is a structural dependence classification relevant to stratified or joint exact inference. Its proof requires nontrivial composition covariance, mixture-of-orientations, and strict polynomial inequalities rather than a routine marginal-moment calculation. It makes no unsupported power or tail guarantee.
